mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.0%, the S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days tends to be positive due to reduced policy uncertainty and lower discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) by more than 10,000 in a single month is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as investor sentiment deteriorates on labor market weakness.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10,000 in a single month
failure_condition: In at least 60% of such triggered months, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (p-value > 0.05 in a two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) grows faster than consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) for two consecutive months, it indicates a supply-side surprise that tends to drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 20 such events, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in residential housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as weak housing momentum amplifies recessionary risk perceptions.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In 40% or more of such events, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months during a tightening cycle, it signals labor market resilience that is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5 for two consecutive months and FEDFUNDS increasing
regime_hint: labor market strengthening in tightening cycle
failure_condition: Across 10 such events, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in retail employment (PAYEMS) by over 30,000 jobs in a single month is accompanied by a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days due to expectations of wage pressure and inflationary risks.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >30,000 in a single month
failure_condition: In 70% of such events, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% suggest disinflation is entrenched, which tends to produce a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as rate-cut expectations rise.
failure_condition: Over 50 such events, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by at least 2% in the same month is a double-signal of softening demand and supply constraints, which tends to drive a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥2% AND CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥2% in the same month
failure_condition: In 40 such triggered months, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p-value > 0.05).
